newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Jan-March cement output up 24 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Jan-March cement output up 24 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Croatian cement output in March rose 28 percent on a monthly basis to 170,420 tonnes, daily Vjesnik reported on Tuesday quoting a local industry agent Incema d.o.o.
January-March output totalled 352,299 tonnes, 24 percent higher than in the same period of 1996, it said.
Sales on the Croatian market rose 53 percent to 281,000 tonnes, with the rest exported. Exports shrank 36 percent compared to the same period of last year.
Although largely indebted and in need of modernisation, the cement industry attracted considerable foreign investment due to massive post-war reconstruction.
Official statistics put the value of housing starts and other building contracts this year at 2.6 billion kuna, compared to 1.6 billion in 1996.
Dalmacijacement factory, in which Trioinvest Handels und Verwaltungs AG has a stake, was said to have been top producer in the first quarter with a total output of 148,736 tonnes.
It was followed by the cement plant in Nasice with 95,518 tonnes and the Koromacno plant, a subsidiary of Societe Suisse de Cement Portland, which produced 81,804 tonnes.

The remaining government holding in the cement industry will be offered to beneficiaries of a mass privatisation scheme in exchange for free vouchers later this year. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
